analyzed_vuln.description: The root cause is trusting a dictionary size field parsed from untrusted chunk data (`context->dict_size = sw32_(...)`) without validating that the dictionary bytes are fully contained within the actual compressed chunk boundaries. `initialize_context_decompression()` only checks against the caller-provided `srcsize`, but in this path `frame_decompress_chunk()` passes `chunk_cbytes` from `blosc2_cbuffer_sizes()`, which can be attacker-inflated relative to the real lazychunk buffer length returned by `frame_get_lazychunk()`. As a result, `context->dict_buffer` points near the end of the real buffer and `ZSTD_createDDict()` copies `dict_size` bytes via memcpy, causing an OOB read in `ZSTD_initDDict_internal`.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In `decompress_frame_fuzzer`, attacker-controlled frame bytes are loaded via `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer()`, then each chunk is decompressed through `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk()` -> `frame_decompress_chunk()` -> `blosc2_decompress_ctx()` -> `initialize_context_decompression()`. Trigger requires a crafted chunk with BLOSC2_USEDICT set and forged header fields such that parsed `chunk_cbytes`/dictionary size are consistent enough to pass local checks but exceed the actual bytes available in the lazychunk buffer. Then dictionary creation (`ZSTD_createDDict` by-copy) performs memcpy past the heap allocation, producing the ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.
